en.title: 6 New YA Fantasy Series Arriving in 2026 to Ignite Your TBR
en.summary: Despite shifts in the YA market, fantasy remains a powerful genre for dedicated readers. Get ready to dive into six fresh, magical worlds set to launch in 2026.
en.body:
The landscape of young adult fiction is constantly evolving, but one genre consistently holds its ground: fantasy. While overall YA sales may have seen fluctuations, the demand for immersive worlds, compelling characters, and magical adventures remains steadfast. For readers who grew up with the foundational works of **Ursula K. Le Guin** and continue to seek out new realms, the prospect of fresh YA fantasy series is always exciting. Fortunately, the publishing world isn't shying away from this beloved genre, with a promising lineup of new series slated for release in 2026.

Publishers are gearing up to introduce readers to a variety of fantastical settings and narratives. Among the anticipated launches is **Clíodhna O’Sullivan**’s **Her Hidden Fire** series, which draws inspiration from Irish folklore. This series plunges readers into a world where magic is a privilege of the elite, following a servant girl named Éadha who possesses a forbidden ability that puts her life in peril. She finds herself entangled in a dangerous class divide, needing to protect the heir to a ruling family, Ionáin, who is also in danger due to his own magical struggles. The second book, **Her Rising Flame**, has already been released, continuing Éadha's perilous journey.

## A Glimpse into 2026's Magical Offerings

Beyond **Her Hidden Fire**, the horizon for 2026 is bright with new series from diverse voices. **Amber Chen**’s **An Auction of Souls** promises intrigue as Meng Lingxi and her grandmother manage an auction house, facing catastrophic events after a mysterious customer arrives. **Gabrielle Landi**’s **A Hearthful of Hatchlings** is set to explore a world where planetary alignments signal a final reckoning, featuring heroes defending their homeworlds against overwhelming odds in a galaxy of magic and advanced weaponry. **Allison Saft**’s **Immortal Game** is another highly anticipated title, offering a fresh take from a beloved author. Further adding to the excitement are **Rachel Griffin**’s **The Sun and the Starmaker**, **Emily Varga**’s **The River She Became**, and **Victoria Carbol**’s **A Great and Powerful Tyranny**. The year also brings **Amanda Foody** and **C. L. Herman**’s **A Fate So Cold**, **Sarah J. Maas**’s **A Court of Splintered Harmony**, **Amal El-Mohtar**’s **Seasons of Glass and Iron: Stories**, **Lex Croucher**’s **The Unmagical Life of Briar Jones**, and **S.C. Bandreddi**’s **The Game of Oaths**. These titles span a range of subgenres, from romantic fantasies to dark academia and historical settings, ensuring something for every fantasy enthusiast.

## Why This Matters to Fantasy Fans

The continued investment in YA fantasy series by publishers is a positive sign for a dedicated global readership. It means that the next generation of readers will have their own enduring magical worlds and relatable characters to champion, fostering a lifelong love for storytelling. This influx of new series offers opportunities to explore diverse cultural mythologies and introduce fresh perspectives within familiar fantasy tropes, enriching the genre for both avid readers and curious newcomers alike. The anticipation building around these 2026 releases signals a vibrant future for YA fantasy, promising epic adventures and unforgettable characters.

## What's Next

As 2026 approaches, keep an eye on official release dates and cover reveals for these exciting new series. Many are expected to launch throughout the year, with specific months announced for titles like **A Hearthful of Hatchlings** in September and potentially others like **Fallen Beauty** by **Astrid Scholte** in November. The full scope of these magical worlds will unfold in the coming months.

content_raw: Though young adult fiction sales have declined compared to the last decade, fantasy as a genre remains one of the genres with the most dedicated readership, regardless of whether it’s YA or adult. Growing up with plenty of classic YA fantasy books, such as those by Ursula K. Le Guin, I wouldn’t be able to imagine a world without YA fantasy just because YA isn’t performing like it once was. As someone who’s familiar with current publishing trends, I am fearful that publishers will cut back on publishing YA books, or that they will slash publication in certain genres in order to follow trends. I wouldn’t want a future where the younger generation won’t have their own classic YA fantasy favorites and magical worlds to discover as they grow up. Luckily, we’re far from that worst-case scenario. If you’re on the lookout for a new fantasy YA series that launched (and will launch) in 2026, and fresh, new worlds to delve into, I’ve got six new YA fantasy series to add to your TBR. Her Hidden Fire series by Clíodhna O’Sullivan In this Irish-inspired fantasy, magic is only for the elite. Éadha, a servant girl, is not supposed to wield magic. This rare ability puts her life at risk as she’s thrust into a world with a class divide. Ionáin, the heir to the ruling family of Ailm’s Keep, should be able to cast magic himself, but this failure somehow puts him in danger. Éadha, who loves Ionáin, must save him and the Keep. The second book in the series, Her Rising Flame , was published earlier this month. It picks up where the first book left off, with Éadha on the run for her life. An Auction of Souls series by Amber Chen Meng Lingxi and her grandmother manage an auction house, and the arrival of a mysterious customer brings about catastrophic events. Meng Lingxi’s grandmother suddenly vanishes, and all that she’s ever known about her life changes. To make matters worse, Meng Lingxi finds out that her grandmother is a servant to the god of the Underworld, and their auction house serves as a portal to hell. To stage a rescue mission, she embarks on a dangerous journey with the help of unlikely allies. Gilded Moon series by Allie Nguyen In Blood of Silver , Linh’s mother has recently died when a strange and mysterious boy pays her a visit, and her life takes a turn for the worse. The boy reveals himself to be the Crown Prince of a magical world called Ebrirene and tells Linh about her mother’s past. She learns that her mother sealed a doorway many years ago that locked out demons. Now, Ebrirene is under attack from these same creatures. The visitor believes that Linh has the power to fortify the portal and seal it forever. The fate of Ebrirene now rests in her hands. River & Salt series by Emily Varga The River She Became follows Yasema, a scholar to the Empire, who secretly reclaims stolen fae relics and uses their power to restore magic to her dying lands.
